children: The $115 bln banking upstart won a provisional US licence after months of regulatory wrangling and is now pushing into business lending. But bulking up its balance sheet with credit could sink its tech-like valuation. Ahead of a planned IPO, lending needs to be slow and steady.
Full view will be published shortly.

On September 3, UK-headquartered fintech Revolut said it received conditional approval from the US Office ‌of the Comptroller of the Currency for a national bank charter – a major step in launching an American bank.

Revolut’s US CEO, Cetin Duransoy, told Reuters that the group now expects a green light from the FDIC ​and Federal Reserve for the banking operations, which are scheduled to launch in the first half of 2027.
Revolut secured a banking license in France in August as part of its European expansion. ​It received authorisation from the Prudential Regulation Authority to operate as ​a bank in the UK in March.

On September 12, the group confirmed that sensitive customer information was disclosed to an unauthorised third party after it received fraudulent requests from a legitimate government agency email domain. "Upon detection, we immediately blocked the address and alerted the relevant government agency as well as enforcement agencies, data protection, and financial regulators," said a company spokesperson.
